newsitem.title: FRANCE: Greenpeace, in money crunch, scales back in France.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace, in money crunch, scales back in France.

text.p: Greenpeace-France, a long-time thorn in the side of the government on environmental controversies, is reducing its activities and laying off more than a third of its staff because of a cash crisis, the group said on Friday.

Executive director Penelope Komites said five of 13 staff positions were being eliminated and the group would limit its focus, concentrating primarily on continuing campaigns against nuclear power and genetically engineered agricultural products.

"We have had a steady increase in contributions over the past five years but our costs have gone up even more," Komites told Reuters. "This does not signal a decline in popularity but is more a reflection of economic hard times."
In 1995 and 1996, the group fell short by about a million francs ($180,000) a year in its annual budget of some 10 million francs ($1.8 million), she said.
Greenpeace has rattled the authorities on a broad range of environmental issues ranging from genetic engineering to clean drinking water.
Greenpeace-International, including Greenpeace-France, generated the most sparks with its high-profile campaign against France's series of six nuclear tests conducted in 1995-96.

The group launched a fierce public relations campaign that triggered informal boycotts of French goods around the world. It also sent boats to the South Pacific to dog the military crews staging the tests.

A decade before, in June 1985, French secret agents had sunk the Greenpeace ship Rainbow Warrior in Auckland harbour, killing a Portuguese photographer who had been sleeping on board, as the vessel prepared to protest against earlier French nuclear tests.

The organisation closed its offices in France for four years after its membership collapsed over the Rainbow Warrior incident. The group's leaders blamed the French secret services, accusing them of launching a smear campaign against it.
Other campaigns have centred on blocking imports of genetically modified maize, closing down a nuclear processing plant in La Hague and ending nuclear waste shipments.
